# Weekly Market Briefing — October 18, 2026

## 1. Market Regime
The backdrop is **cautiously risk-off beneath the surface**. The curve remains normal and upward-sloping (10Y-3M at **+1.03 pts**), but both ends have crept higher MoM — the 10Y at **5.1% (▲0.09)** and the 3M bill at **4.07% (▲0.1)**. VIX ticked up to **19.99 (▲2.28)** — still "normal," not panic — while the **DXY firmed to 101.84 (▲1.62)**, consistent with higher-for-longer rate pricing. Broad-market factors confirm defensiveness: SPY scores Low-Vol **69** vs. Momentum **49**, DIA **76/40**, and IWM leans deep-Value (**91**) but weak-Momentum (**31**). The tone is stable headline indices masking a rotation away from high-beta growth.

## 2. This Week's News
The week was defined by a hot inflation print colliding with an AI-trade unwind. September CPI came in at 3.7% year-on-year (expected 3.6%, August 3.4%), with core at 2.6% and headline up 0.6% month-on-month. PPI climbed 1.3% month-on-month, the largest single-month gain since March 2022, while retail sales grew 0.8%, showing consumer resilience. Despite this, the 10-year yield eased to 5.10%, down from 5.24% on Oct 9, and the S&P 500 ended ~0.86% below its Oct 9 close. The bigger story was semiconductors: US chip stocks lost roughly $1.64 trillion in market value over six sessions on concerns about AI spending, corporate debt and higher rates. Broadcom and Intel executives warned that financing could become a major AI headwind — Broadcom's Hock Tan calling it potentially a bigger challenge than chip or electricity shortages. On policy, the base case is a hawkish hold — the Fed keeps rates steady on Oct 28 and leaves the door open for a December hike.

## 3. Factor Leadership
**Defensives and Value are being rewarded; Momentum is bifurcated.** Energy (XLE) is the standout, leading on Value (**80**), Momentum (**87**) and Low-Vol (**91**) with 12-1 momentum of **54.2%**. Defensive sleeves rank highest on Low-Vol — Staples XLP **96**, Health Care XLV **86**, Real Estate XLRE **89** — while rate-sensitive Utilities (XLU) carry high Value (**85**) but the weakest Momentum (**13**). Dividend/quality names are leading: ABBV (Value **98**, Quality **80**), and CVX (Value **83**, Growth **88**).

## 4. Notable Movers
- **AMD** — Momentum **100** and 12-1 of **138.7%**, but Low-Vol **4** and Vol% **33.6**: a crowded high-beta name squarely in the AI crosshairs.
- **LINK-USD / AVAX-USD / SOL-USD** — crypto momentum extremes (**96/94/93**) paired with rock-bottom Low-Vol scores.
- **Overbought (RSI>70):** KO (76), PG (75), XLP (73), XOM/ABBV/CVX (71-73).
- **Deeply oversold (RSI<30):** none, but QQQ (35), NVDA (38), AMD (38), SNOW (37) sit near the low end amid the chip rout.
- **Unusual combos:** PLTR (Growth **100**, Quality **96**, but Value **2**); NFLX (Momentum **2**, 12-1 of **-39.3%**) amid reported layoffs.

## 5. Themes to Watch
Monitor the **Oct 27–28 FOMC** against sticky inflation, the AI/credit narrative (CoreWeave debt, memory oversupply), and heavyweight earnings — next week the market shifts focus to Q3 earnings, with Tesla and Meta in view. Watch whether the dollar and 10Y resume climbing, and if VIX breaks above the "normal" regime.

*No buy/sell recommendations — see the monthly report.*
